record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: Improve the current O(N^5) upper bound for computing the weighted straight skeleton of a polygon, possibly by exploiting deeper structural properties of the associated Stable Roommates instance used in the reduction.

evidence.quote: They conjectured that this running time can be improved. A deeper insight into the structure of the underlying sr instance might lead to such an improvement in the efficiency of the algorithm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with N vertices, where each edge e of P is assigned a positive real weight w(e). The weighted straight skeleton of P is defined by the following continuous wavefront propagation: each edge translates inward (into the interior of P) in the direction of its inward normal at speed w(e); adjacent moving edges remain incident at their shared moving vertex, while topological events (edge events, in which a wavefront edge collapses, and split events, in which a reflex wavefront vertex hits a wavefront edge) modify the wavefront combinatorially. The traces of the wavefront vertices over time form a planar straight-line graph inside P called the weighted straight skeleton of (P, w).

There is a known algorithm that computes the weighted straight skeleton of (P, w) in worst-case time O(N^5), where the bottleneck is a reduction to a Stable Roommates instance (in which the candidate pairings of wavefront elements are encoded as preference lists, and selecting the next event corresponds to finding a stable matching).

Problem. Design an algorithm that computes the weighted straight skeleton of an arbitrary simple polygon with weighted edges in worst-case time strictly better than O(N^5), ideally by exploiting structural properties of the associated Stable Roommates instance arising from the geometric reduction.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface algorithms for (unweighted/positively-weighted) straight skeletons with bounds such as O(n^3 log n), motorcycle-graph–based subcubic bounds, and recent predictor–corrector constructions, but no source explicitly improves the O(N^5) bound that arises specifically from the Stable Roommates–based reduction for weighted straight skeletons. The status of the specific improvement asked here could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: A universal predictor-corrector type incremental algorithm for the construction of weighted straight skeletons
status_evidence.snippet: Incremental algorithm for weighted straight skeletons; does not claim to beat the O(N^5) Stable Roommates–based bound for general weighted polygons.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on weighted straight skeleton construction does not report an improvement specifically over the O(N^5) Stable Roommates reduction bound.

status_evidence.title: Weighted straight skeletons (research page)
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the reduction of the planar matching problem for weighted straight skeletons to a Stable Roommates instance.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the existence of the Stable Roommates–based approach underlying the O(N^5) bound.

status_evidence.title: A Faster Algorithm for Computing Straight Skeletons
status_evidence.snippet: Faster algorithms exist for unweighted straight skeletons via motorcycle graphs, but these results do not address the weighted O(N^5) bound.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements known in the unweighted case do not directly resolve the weighted-case complexity question.
